+\begin{corollary}\leanok
+[Defining property of the Hilbert polynomial]
+  \label{cor:hilbertPolynomial_eval_eventually}
+  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.hilbertPolynomial_eval_eventually}
+  \uses{def:hilbert_polynomial, def:fiber_hilbert_function,
+    lem:hilbertPolynomial_unique}
+  % ENCODING. Scheme.hilbertPolynomial_eval_eventually. Sorry-free in
+  % AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/HilbertPolynomial.lean.
+  Let \(h_{\mathcal{F},s}\) be the graded Hilbert function of
+  \cref{def:fiber_hilbert_function}. If \emph{some} polynomial in
+  \(\mathbb{Q}[\lambda]\) agrees with \(h_{\mathcal{F},s}\) at all
+  sufficiently large integers, then the Hilbert polynomial
+  \(\Phi_{\mathcal{F},s}\) of \cref{def:hilbert_polynomial} does:
+  \(\Phi_{\mathcal{F},s}(m) = h_{\mathcal{F},s}(m)\) for all \(m \gg 0\).
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+  \uses{def:hilbert_polynomial, lem:hilbertPolynomial_unique}
+  \leanok
+  Let \(\Psi \in \mathbb{Q}[\lambda]\) agree with \(h_{\mathcal{F},s}\) at all
+  \(m > N\). By \cref{def:hilbert_polynomial} the Hilbert polynomial
+  \(\Phi_{\mathcal{F},s}\) is a polynomial agreeing with
+  \(h_{\mathcal{F},s}\) for all \(m \gg 0\) whenever one exists, and by
+  \cref{lem:hilbertPolynomial_unique} any such polynomial is unique, so
+  \(\Phi_{\mathcal{F},s} = \Psi\); hence
+  \(\Phi_{\mathcal{F},s}(m) = h_{\mathcal{F},s}(m)\) for all \(m > N\).
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}\leanok
+[The Hilbert polynomial under a rational Hilbert function]
+  \label{cor:hilbertPolynomial_eval_of_isRatHilb}
+  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.hilbertPolynomial_eval_of_isRatHilb}
+  \uses{def:hilbert_polynomial, def:ratHilb, lem:hilbertPoly_of_isRatHilb,
+    cor:hilbertPolynomial_eval_eventually}
+  % ENCODING. Scheme.hilbertPolynomial_eval_of_isRatHilb. Sorry-free in
+  % AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/HilbertPolynomial.lean.
+  If the graded Hilbert function \(h_{\mathcal{F},s}\) is a rational Hilbert
+  function of some order \(d\) (\cref{def:ratHilb}), then the Hilbert
+  polynomial \(\Phi_{\mathcal{F},s}\) of \cref{def:hilbert_polynomial}
+  satisfies \(\Phi_{\mathcal{F},s}(m) = h_{\mathcal{F},s}(m)\) for all
+  \(m \gg 0\).
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+  \uses{lem:hilbertPoly_of_isRatHilb, cor:hilbertPolynomial_eval_eventually}
+  \leanok
+  By \cref{lem:hilbertPoly_of_isRatHilb} some polynomial agrees with
+  \(h_{\mathcal{F},s}\) at all sufficiently large integers; conclude by
+  \cref{cor:hilbertPolynomial_eval_eventually}.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}\leanok
+[The Hilbert polynomial computes as the extracted numerator polynomial]
+  \label{cor:hilbertPolynomial_eq_hilbertPoly}
+  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.hilbertPolynomial_eq_hilbertPoly}
+  \uses{def:hilbert_polynomial, def:ratHilb, lem:hilbertPoly_exists_mathlib,
+    lem:hilbertPolynomial_unique}
+  % ENCODING. Scheme.hilbertPolynomial_eq_hilbertPoly: under an explicit
+  % rational-series presentation of the graded Hilbert function,
+  % hilbertPolynomial π L F s = Polynomial.hilbertPoly p d. Sorry-free in
+  % AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/HilbertPolynomial.lean.
+  Suppose there are \(p \in \mathbb{Q}[X]\) and \(d, N \in \mathbb{N}\) with
+  \(h_{\mathcal{F},s}(m) = [X^m]\bigl(p \cdot (1-X)^{-d}\bigr)\) for all
+  \(m > N\) (\cref{def:ratHilb}). Then the Hilbert polynomial of
+  \cref{def:hilbert_polynomial} is the polynomial extracted from the pair
+  \((p, d)\) by \cref{lem:hilbertPoly_exists_mathlib}:
+  \(\Phi_{\mathcal{F},s} = \mathrm{hilbertPoly}\,p\,d\).
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+  \uses{lem:hilbertPoly_exists_mathlib, lem:hilbertPolynomial_unique}
+  \leanok
+  By \cref{lem:hilbertPoly_exists_mathlib} there is an \(N'\) with
+  \((\mathrm{hilbertPoly}\,p\,d)(n) = [X^n](p\cdot(1-X)^{-d})\) for all
+  \(n > N'\), so \(\mathrm{hilbertPoly}\,p\,d\) agrees with
+  \(h_{\mathcal{F},s}\) at all \(m > \max(N, N')\). Both
+  \(\Phi_{\mathcal{F},s}\) and \(\mathrm{hilbertPoly}\,p\,d\) therefore agree
+  with \(h_{\mathcal{F},s}\) at all sufficiently large integers, and
+  \cref{lem:hilbertPolynomial_unique} gives
+  \(\Phi_{\mathcal{F},s} = \mathrm{hilbertPoly}\,p\,d\).
+\end{proof}
